header.running_head: 3. The Rights and Duties of Muslims

blocks.tamil_translation: (I was surprised that Rasulullah ﷺ had given such great good news about him, yet he had no such special deed!”) I said to him, “O servant of Allah! There is no anger between me and my father, nor any disagreement. I heard Rasulullah ﷺ say (about you) three times, “A man from the people of Jannah is about to come to you now.” All three times it was you who came. I thought that I would come and stay with you, see your particular deed, and follow you. I did not see you doing many deeds. What is the particular deed because of which you attained the rank the Prophet ﷺ spoke of? (you must now tell me) This is what really happened,” I said. “(I have no such particular deed at all.) There are no deeds other than the ones you saw,” said that Ansari Sahabi. Hazrat Abdullah ibn Amr (RA) says, (after hearing this I turned back) As I began to turn away from him, he called me and said, “My deeds are only what you saw, but my habit is that there is no deceit in my heart towards any Muslim. And if Allah Ta'ala has given someone special blessings, I do not envy him on seeing it.” Hazrat Abdullah (RA) said, “It is because of this habit that you attained that rank, and this is a thing we are unable to do.” Hazrat Anas ibn Malik (RA) narrates that Hazrat Abdullah ibn Amr (RA) would often relate this incident of staying with that Ansari Sahabi.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ اَبِيْ هُرَيْرَةَ ﵁ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُوْلُ اللهِ ﷺ: مَنْ وَسَّعَ عَلَي
